summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update32.json → valid=true). Sharpened the heartbeat-admission finding by working out the counterfactual. The previous record established the asymmetry — the general RPC path refuses a peer more than one version behind before dispatch, the heartbeat fast path applies no version check and so honours such a peer's heartbeats — and this successor shows what that costs a cluster rather than one node. A follower's only route back to progress is its heartbeat timeout, measured from the last contact that an accepted message refreshed, after which it clears the leader record and campaigns (raft.go:219-245); the fast path is fed precisely by messages that qualify as heartbeats by their empty field pattern (net_transport.go:668-684) and accepts them without the version check (raft.go:1415-1436), so the contact record is kept fresh by the very peer whose entry-bearing messages are refused before dispatch. The timeout therefore never fires, no election starts, and the cluster stays pinned to a leader that cannot deliver entries — whereas with a uniform version check the refused messages would have left contact stale and the voters would have timed out and elected a compatible leader themselves. So the consequence is larger than 'one follower cannot catch up': it is the loss of automatic recovery from an incompatible leader. Recorded as one Fact plus a successor interpretation for the same question (earlier interpretation and counterevidence preserved) with the conclusion kept conditional, because the situation needs a version gap wider than the library's documented support window and the incompatible node to be the leader, and because an operator can still repair it by removing or restarting that node; counterevidence also notes that the stall lasts only while the incompatible node keeps heartbeating, and that nothing was executed.
